surgery.name: Surgery & Procedures
surgery.summary: From routine spays to complex soft-tissue surgery.
surgery.description: Our surgical suite is equipped for everything from routine sterilizations to complex soft-tissue and emergency procedures, with full pre-anaesthetic screening and dedicated post-op monitoring for every patient.

spay-neuter-cat.name: Spay / Neuter — Cat
spay-neuter-cat.description: Routine cat sterilization with pre-anaesthetic bloodwork and take-home pain plan.

spay-neuter-dog.name: Spay / Neuter — Dog
spay-neuter-dog.description: Routine dog sterilization with pre-anaesthetic bloodwork and take-home pain plan.

soft-tissue-surgery.name: Soft-Tissue Surgery
soft-tissue-surgery.description: Mass removals, wound repair, and abdominal procedures.

post-op-care-plan.name: Post-Op Care Plan
post-op-care-plan.description: Suture check, pain management review, and recovery monitoring.

richContent.intro: We offer a complete range of surgical services, from minor procedures to complex operations. Our surgical suite is equipped with the latest technology to help ensure safety and successful outcomes.

sections.heading: Before your surgery
sections.body: Your pet needs a clean bill of health before a routine operation — we typically confirm this with bloodwork a few days beforehand. Please have your pet fast from midnight the night before (feeding schedules differ for kittens, puppies, and rabbits — just ask). Drop-off is between 7:45–8:00 AM; you'll fill out a short intake form on arrival, and dogs should have had a chance to relieve themselves first.

bullets.label: Tumor surgery
bullets.detail: Gentle removal of benign and malignant tumors, with careful aftercare.

bullets.label: Reconstructive surgery
bullets.detail: Restoring function and appearance after injury using advanced techniques.

bullets.label: Abdominal surgery
bullets.detail: Emergency and planned procedures — e.g. bloat, uterine infection, or intestinal issues.

sections.heading: How we prepare, monitor, and recover your pet

bullets.label: Preparation
bullets.detail: A thorough health check and a conversation with you about every option before the procedure.

bullets.label: Monitoring
bullets.detail: Continuous monitoring by experienced veterinarians and licensed veterinary nurses, with modern anaesthesia techniques to minimize risk and stress.

bullets.label: Aftercare
bullets.detail: Clear at-home care instructions, plus a follow-up to confirm recovery is on track.

preventive-care.name: Primary & Preventive Care
preventive-care.summary: Vaccinations, wellness exams, and puppy & kitten checks.
preventive-care.description: The foundation of a long, healthy life — core and lifestyle vaccinations, wellness exams, parasite prevention, microchipping, and health certificates for travel or breed registration.

wellness-exam.name: Wellness Exam
wellness-exam.description: Full nose-to-tail check-up with a licensed veterinarian.

vaccination-cat.name: Vaccination — Cat
vaccination-cat.description: Core vaccines plus rabies add-on, tailored to your cat's lifestyle and risk.

vaccination-dog.name: Vaccination — Dog
vaccination-dog.description: Core vaccines plus rabies add-on, tailored to your dog's lifestyle and risk.

puppy-kitten-starter-visit.name: Puppy & Kitten Starter Visit
puppy-kitten-starter-visit.description: First-visit exam, deworming, and vaccine schedule planning.

microchipping-id.name: Microchipping & ID
microchipping-id.description: Permanent ID chip with registry enrollment.

richContent.intro: A broad range of wellness and primary care services, so your pet feels their best through every life stage — vaccinations, ID chipping, spay/neuter, or advice before travelling abroad, we're here with care tailored to your pet.

sections.heading: Vaccinations for dogs, cats & rabbits
sections.body: We provide all standard vaccinations to protect against infectious disease. For cats: protection against cat flu and panleukopenia (RC/Ducat or RCP/Tricat). For dogs: kennel cough, distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis, and leptospirosis (Pi, KC, DHPPi). Rabbits can be protected against myxomatosis and RHD via Myxo-RHD PLUS.

sections.heading: Spay & neuter
sections.body: We neuter and spay dogs, cats, rabbits, and guinea pigs of either sex — supporting calmer behavior, lower disease risk, and fewer unplanned litters.

sections.heading: ID chipping & EU pet passports
sections.body: To identify your pet while travelling, if lost, or for registration, we offer both microchipping and tattoo ID. We also help issue an EU pet passport — required for travel within and outside the EU — which records ID and rabies vaccination details.

sections.heading: Health checks & nail trims
sections.body: We offer veterinary exams for adult pets and puppies/kittens, with or without vaccination and chipping — especially useful before a sale or for insurance. We're also happy to help with nail trims.

sections.heading: Reproduction & pregnancy checks
sections.body: Progesterone testing ahead of breeding, and pregnancy checks to support a safe, healthy reproductive process.

sections.heading: A gentle goodbye
sections.body: When it's time to say goodbye, we offer a calm, respectful farewell — including cremation, individual or shared, with the option of an urn. You'll have a private room on arrival and a separate exit if you'd rather avoid the main waiting area on your way out.

dental.name: Dental Services
dental.summary: Tartar removal, dental X-rays, and extractions.
dental.description: Dental disease affects most pets by age three. We offer ultrasonic scaling and polishing, full-mouth dental radiographs, and extractions under monitored anaesthesia.

dental-cleaning-polish.name: Dental Cleaning & Polish
dental-cleaning-polish.description: Ultrasonic scaling and polishing under anaesthesia.

dental-x-rays.name: Dental X-Rays
dental-x-rays.description: Full-mouth radiographs to catch disease below the gumline.

tooth-extraction.name: Tooth Extraction
tooth-extraction.description: Simple to surgical extractions with pain management.

richContent.intro: Dental health is a key part of your pet's overall wellbeing. We offer a complete range of dental services, from preventive cleanings to advanced treatment — just like for us, untreated tooth problems can cause both pain and wider health issues.

sections.heading: Before a dental procedure
sections.body: We'll want a clear picture of your pet's health beforehand, usually confirmed with bloodwork a few days ahead. Your pet should fast from midnight the night before (different timing applies for kittens and puppies). Drop-off is 7:45–8:00 AM with a short intake form, and dogs should be well-exercised beforehand.

bullets.label: Scaling & polishing
bullets.detail: Ultrasonic cleaning to thoroughly remove plaque and tartar, reducing the risk of tooth loss.

bullets.label: Dental X-rays
bullets.detail: Advanced imaging to spot problems below the gumline, like root infections or fractures.

bullets.label: Extractions
bullets.detail: Safe, gentle removal for infected, damaged, or unsalvageable teeth.

bullets.label: Periodontal treatment
bullets.detail: Treating gum disease before it spreads and causes further problems.

bullets.label: At-home advice
bullets.detail: Tips and product recommendations for daily dental care, like brushes and chew products.

diagnostics.name: Laboratory & Diagnostics
diagnostics.summary: In-house bloodwork, urinalysis, and rapid test panels.
diagnostics.description: Our in-house lab returns most bloodwork and urinalysis results within the hour, so treatment decisions don't wait on a courier.

bloodwork-panel.name: Bloodwork Panel
bloodwork-panel.description: Complete blood count and chemistry panel, in-house results.

urinalysis.name: Urinalysis
urinalysis.description: Screening for kidney, bladder, and metabolic issues.

rapid-test-panels.name: Rapid Test Panels
rapid-test-panels.description: Parvo, heartworm, tick-borne disease, and FeLV/FIV screening.

richContent.intro: Our in-house laboratory is a key part of how we diagnose and treat quickly. By analyzing samples directly at the clinic, we can often give you answers within the same visit — meaning faster treatment and better care.

sections.heading: Before a lab visit
sections.body: For most blood work, your pet should arrive fasting unless told otherwise, to keep results accurate. Turnaround time varies depending on which values are being tested.

bullets.label: Blood work
bullets.detail: From blood values and organ function to signs of inflammation or infection — a key tool for tracking conditions like kidney disease, diabetes, or hormonal imbalances.

bullets.label: Urine testing
bullets.detail: Identifies kidney and urinary tract disease, infections, and crystals.

bullets.label: Fecal testing
bullets.detail: Detects parasites and other gastrointestinal issues.

bullets.label: Cytology & biopsy
bullets.detail: Fast analysis of cells and tissue when we spot a suspicious change in skin or elsewhere.

bullets.label: Infectious disease testing
bullets.detail: Testing for bacteria, viruses, and other organisms to find the underlying cause of illness.

imaging.name: Imaging
imaging.summary: Digital radiography and ultrasound on site.
imaging.description: Digital X-ray and ultrasound equipment on site means faster, clearer answers for injuries, swallowed objects, and internal medicine cases — no referral wait.

digital-radiography.name: Digital Radiography
digital-radiography.description: High-resolution X-ray imaging with same-day read.

abdominal-ultrasound.name: Abdominal Ultrasound
abdominal-ultrasound.description: Non-invasive imaging for organs and soft tissue.

richContent.intro: X-ray and ultrasound are essential tools in modern veterinary care. We've invested in the latest imaging technology, so we can examine everything from skeletal injuries to organ function without more invasive methods.

bullets.label: High-quality digital imaging
bullets.detail: Fast results identifying fractures, joint problems, or lung and heart conditions.

bullets.label: Foreign object detection
bullets.detail: Especially useful when something's been swallowed — we can quickly locate it and plan safe next steps.

bullets.label: Organ imaging
bullets.detail: A gentle way to examine the liver, kidneys, bladder, and heart.

bullets.label: Pregnancy checks
bullets.detail: Confirming pregnancy and monitoring fetal development.

bullets.label: Disease investigation
bullets.detail: Getting a clear picture of tumors or fluid buildup to help plan treatment.

orthopedics.name: Orthopedics
orthopedics.summary: ACL injuries, fracture repair, and spinal care.
orthopedics.description: From cranial cruciate ligament injuries to fracture stabilization and spinal cases, our orthopedic service pairs surgical expertise with a structured rehab plan.

orthopedic-consultation.name: Orthopedic Consultation
orthopedic-consultation.description: Lameness exam with imaging referral plan.

cruciate-acl-repair.name: Cruciate (ACL) Repair
cruciate-acl-repair.description: Surgical stabilization for cranial cruciate ligament injuries.

richContent.intro: Orthopedics demands real expertise and specialized equipment — we're proud to offer these services to help improve your pet's quality of life.

bullets.label: Fractures & injuries
bullets.detail: Careful diagnosis via X-ray, with treatments including surgical fixation and casting.

bullets.label: Joint problems
bullets.detail: Conditions like hip dysplasia and patellar luxation, treated both surgically and non-surgically.

bullets.label: Arthritis & degenerative conditions
bullets.detail: Pain management and rehabilitation plans to improve mobility.

sections.heading: Cruciate ligament injuries
sections.body: A common condition in dogs and cats, causing pain and reduced mobility. We use modern equipment to confirm the diagnosis, and perform an arthroscopic exam alongside TPLO surgery to fully assess the joint and plan treatment.

sections.heading: Disc herniation
sections.body: A serious condition, mostly affecting dogs, where a disc between the vertebrae is damaged or displaced. We're proud to be one of the few clinics that performs disc herniation surgery — we assess the extent of the damage and recommend the treatment that fits your pet best.

endoscopy.name: Endoscopy
endoscopy.summary: Minimally invasive scoping for scopes & swallowed objects.
endoscopy.description: Bronchoscopy and gastroscopy let us investigate chronic coughing, swallowing difficulty, or a suspected foreign body without open surgery in many cases.

gastroscopy.name: Gastroscopy
gastroscopy.description: Camera-guided exam of the oesophagus and stomach.

bronchoscopy.name: Bronchoscopy
bronchoscopy.description: Airway scoping for chronic cough or breathing issues.

foreign-body-retrieval.name: Foreign Body Retrieval
foreign-body-retrieval.description: Non-surgical removal of swallowed objects where possible.

richContent.intro: Bronchoscopy and gastroscopy let us examine and treat the airways and GI tract without major surgery — gentler on your pet, with a faster recovery.

sections.heading: Bronchoscopy
sections.body: Used to examine the airways and lungs when we suspect chronic coughing or breathing difficulty, an inhaled foreign object, or a suspected infection or tumor. We use a thin, flexible camera to see inside the airways while removing objects or collecting samples for analysis.

sections.heading: Gastroscopy
sections.body: Used to examine and treat the esophagus, stomach, and upper small intestine — for swallowing problems or suspected blockages, ulcers, inflammation, or tumors, and to retrieve swallowed foreign objects.

emergency.name: Emergency Care
emergency.description: Accidents don't wait for an appointment. We prioritize acute cases for same-day stabilization and treatment, with an after-hours line for existing clients.

after-hours-consultation.name: After-Hours Consultation
after-hours-consultation.description: Phone triage line for existing clients.

richContent.intro: We're here when you need us — emergency care is available daily during our opening hours for injuries, wounds, and urgent procedures.

sections.heading: Please call before you come in
sections.body: For urgent cases, always call us first. That lets us assess the situation, prepare staff, and make sure we're ready to receive your pet the moment you arrive.

sections.heading: How we handle urgent cases
sections.body: For symptoms like diarrhea, vomiting, or sudden skin issues, we have a dedicated isolation area to limit the spread of illness. Some wait time can occur during busy periods, but life-threatening conditions are always prioritized. We can also offer daytime inpatient monitoring when needed.

essential.name: Essential
essential.tagline: For healthy pets that just need the basics covered.

wellness.name: Wellness Plus
wellness.tagline: Our most popular plan for ongoing preventive care.

complete.name: Complete Care
complete.tagline: Comprehensive coverage for senior pets or multi-pet households.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.body: Quick answers to what pet owners ask us most. Can't find what you're looking for? Reach out and we'll help directly.

tick-prescription.question: How do I get a prescription for tick medication?
tick-prescription.answer: We can issue preventive prescriptions, such as tick medication, by email or phone — no in-person visit needed. Our only requirement is that your pet has been seen at the clinic at some point during the year. Note it can take a couple of days before the prescription is ready for pickup at the pharmacy.

cat-neuter-age.question: At what age can I neuter my cat?
cat-neuter-age.answer: Cats are typically neutered at around 5 to 6 months old. That's a good window — old enough to safely undergo the procedure, but young enough to avoid unwanted behaviors that can appear with sexual maturity. It's always worth discussing timing with a veterinarian for advice specific to your cat.

fever.question: How do I know if my pet has a fever?
fever.answer: A few signs to watch for: temperature — the most reliable method is a digital rectal thermometer, normal is typically 38–39°C for cats and dogs; behavior changes — more tired, less active, or sleeping more than usual; appetite — a sudden drop can be a warning sign; body language — excessive licking, hiding, or reacting negatively to touch; breathing — faster or labored breathing can also indicate fever or illness. If you suspect a fever or illness, it's best to contact a veterinarian for advice and a possible exam.

diarrhea.question: My dog has diarrhea. What should I do?
diarrhea.answer: Watch the symptoms — note how long it's been going on and whether there are other signs like vomiting, low appetite, lethargy, or blood. Reduce food intake — offer small portions of something easy to digest, like rice with boiled chicken or white fish, over the following days. Make sure your dog is drinking enough water, offering a pet-specific electrolyte solution if needed. If diarrhea continues past 24–48 hours, or you see blood or signs of dehydration, contact a veterinarian. See a vet sooner if your dog is very young, senior, or has other health conditions.

overweight.question: Does it matter if my pet is a little overweight?
overweight.answer: Yes — even a little extra weight can make a difference. It can contribute to diabetes, joint problems, and heart disease. A veterinarian can advise on diet and exercise, and regular check-ups plus a balanced diet can meaningfully improve your pet's quality of life.

cough.question: My dog has a cough. What should I do?
cough.answer: Start by observing closely — note any other signs like fever, tiredness, low appetite, or nasal discharge. It's best to book a veterinary exam, since coughing can come from several causes, including infections, allergies, or heart issues. Keep your dog calm and avoid strenuous activity until you know the cause, and follow your vet's guidance closely if treatment is prescribed.

heat-cycle.question: How often does a female dog go into heat?
heat-cycle.answer: On average, every six to twelve months, with each cycle lasting around 2–3 weeks. This varies between individual dogs, so some cycles run longer or shorter than others. If you have specific questions about your dog's cycle, it's worth checking in with a veterinarian.

neuter-pros-cons.question: What are the pros and cons of neutering?
neuter-pros-cons.answer: Benefits: fewer unplanned litters; can reduce aggression and territorial behavior in males and certain behaviors in females; lowers the risk of certain diseases; neutered pets tend to live longer on average. Considerations: like any surgery, there's a small risk of complications; metabolism can shift, so weight gain is possible if diet isn't adjusted; personality or energy level can shift in some cases. Worth discussing these factors with a veterinarian to make an informed choice for your pet.

vomiting-cat.question: My cat vomits often. Is that normal?
vomiting-cat.answer: Occasional vomiting isn't unusual in cats, but it's worth paying attention to how often it happens. Common causes: hairballs from grooming, eating too fast or too much, food sensitivities, or — less commonly — an underlying illness. If your cat vomits frequently, or you notice other symptoms like diarrhea, lethargy, or appetite changes, it's worth a veterinary visit for a proper assessment.

prescription-no-visit.question: Can I get a prescription without coming in for a visit?
prescription-no-visit.answer: We can issue preventive prescriptions, like tick medication, by email or phone. Other prescriptions require a veterinary visit. Pets on ongoing medication typically need to be seen once a year for us to keep renewing prescriptions.
